rows.reason: Correctly rejects the 50x premise via Amdahl, insists on tracing first, and gives a falsifiable decision procedure, though the cheap-fix list runs a little long.
Names selection bias directly, checks the blended-retention arithmetic correctly, and proposes an intent-to-treat holdout with an early proxy metric; tight and actionable.
Rejects the 95.1% headline, sizes the max-of-200 inflation correctly (~1.3 pts at n=2000), and flags the untuned baseline; concise.
Accurate break-even-under-dilution, liquidation-waterfall and log-utility calculations, plus the 5% reliability and board-duty points, ending in a staged test; excellent.
Short and correct: measure first, gives a sound Amdahl-based threshold (>70% waiting means well under 2x), and an incremental path if CPU-bound.
Covers concave utility, the unverified 5% against base rates, preferences, dilution and board authority, and recommends a cheap test plus asking for an extension; solid.
Correct selection-inflation estimate, flags the untuned baseline, recommends fresh held-out data or nested CV, and gives paper wording.
Rejects the clean-test framing with correct noise arithmetic and good options, but the closing spread diagnostic gets the logic muddled (a wide spread does not make the max more lottery-like).
Correct Amdahl example (1.24x), specific profiling steps with py-spy and query logs, and a cheap single-endpoint experiment; well proportioned.
Explains the selection gap clearly, notes the 90-day result can't be read until late January, and recommends an ITT randomized holdout or a 50% flag rollout.

Thorough and numerically correct log-utility and discounting tables plus waterfall, dilution, 5% reliability and fiduciary points; long, and discounting an already probability-weighted EV at a venture rate partly double-counts risk.
Correct illustrative arithmetic, good points on denominator shrinkage, experienced-user skippers and completion timing, and a holdout with pre-registered range and guardrails.
Correct peeking inflation figures (~14-19%), explains winner's curse, and gives SRM, guardrail and sequential-method fixes; clear and actionable.
Covers peeking, winner's curse, weekday coverage and the relative-vs-absolute lift question, and adds a nice A/A simulation check; the 15-30% range is a bit loose for six looks.

Concise and correct on inflation and effect bias, rebuts the Bayesian escape well, and gives a concrete holdout plan; the 'one-in-seven event' phrasing loosely conflates procedure error rate with the p-value.
Clear no, with honest in-progress wording, a cheap posting audit, and a sharp rebuttal of the everyone-inflates argument; proportionate.

Correct no with honest wording options and a project emphasis; sound but fairly generic and somewhat repetitive.

Correct and comprehensive (Amdahl, causes, rewrite costs, quarter plan) but padded, and it asserts an unsourced 'often 1.5 to 3x' end-to-end gain figure.

Rejects the all-in moonshot with correct log-utility certainty equivalents, discounting, waterfall, dilution, 5%-reliability and fiduciary points, plus a staged alternative; somewhat long but numerically sound.
Clearly identifies selection bias, gate effects and the uncheckable 90-day horizon, and prescribes an intention-to-treat randomized rollout concisely.
